vignette: Say goodbye to runner’s knees and jogging’s stress fractures. Instead, enjoy what is fast becoming the exercise of choice: walking. It’s fun, easy and inexpensive. Walking is the most underrated exercise in the world,” says Dr. Wells, an Arizona State University Professor. Wells advocates walking for a number of reasons. It is invigorating, yet nowhere near as exhausting as jogging or running. And walkers are less likely to get injured than joggers. Almost anyone can take up walking, including people with low back-pain-complaints. As an exercise, walking can even be recuperative. What’s more, it allows you to go at your own pace, while getting you out in the fresh air. Walking is of benefit because it is an aerobic exercise, like running, swimming, cross-country skiing and the currently popular aerobic dancing. By increasing the supply of oxygen to the muscles and skin, aerobic exercises help build the body’s capacity for expending energy and physical endurance. In addition, because it strengthens heart and lungs, aerobic exercise is believed to be an important factor in preventing heart disease. The results from walking can be impressive. Forty minutes of brisk walking can burn 300 calories---the same amount you would use in 30 minutes of swimming or running. The faster you walk the more calories you burn. “Striding”----also known as race walking, health walking, and fitness walking----has been shown to reduce blood pressure, lower the heart rate while you are at rest, improve the body’s ability to take in oxygen during exercise and increase the efficiency of the heart and lungs. And, of course, it can use up those excess calories that contribute to obesity. To get a truly beneficial walking workout, however, requires exertion. Indeed, as walkers quickly discover, there is considerable difference between taking a leisurely stroll and walking briskly enough to tone those sagging muscles, burn excess fat and conditionthe heart and lungs. In addition to its many physical benefits, like other physical activities, walking also has a soothing effect on the psyche. It can help you to think more clearly and feel more relaxed, as well as give you a better outlook on life. It also can be a sociable activity. An early morning walk around the neighbourhood provides an opportunity to chat with friends or simply admire the flowers. Or because it does not require a team or even a partner, walking is something you can do on your own time, by yourself, whenever the mood strikes. One of the most important attractions for walking is its long-lasting appeal. Whereas jogging and aerobic dancing can pall quickly, walking provides a popular activity that seems to endure. Fitness Foundations estimate that among the most regular walkers are those 65 years and older----evidence that walking is an exercise that lasts. A large part of walking’s universal appeal is its low-key enjoyment. There is no need to compete with others or to strain for distance or speed. Called the “world’s greatest exercise,” walking is a gentle activity that can convince even the most lethargic among us to begin a fitness regimen.
